narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is shuv read under negation - 'if a man does not repent' - repentance named only in the wicked's refusal of it (7691996). Type (102) is volition: not a felt state nor a deed done but an act of the will, or rather the withholding of that act - the interior declining to turn (7691997). Source (103) is absent: the reading books no origin behind the refusal, tracing the impenitence to no named driver, so the refusal stands as the wicked's own unaccounted posture (present:false). Seat (104) resolves to none: the refusal-to-repent is not organ-located, not lodged in a named inner faculty - it is held by the person as such, not seated in an interior organ (7691998). Bearer (105) is the wicked (inferred, to_span 283588): the interior read is the evildoer of the psalm, the man who conceives evil and gives birth to lies (7691999). Operation (106), the core event, is 'if the wicked man does not turn/repent, God whets his sword - impenitence as the wicked's settled refusal': the movement is a non-movement, the interior fixed against turning while judgment is readied over it (7692000). Target (107) is impenitence (inferred, to_span 283588): what the operation resolves to is the impenitence itself - a refusal aimed at nothing beyond its own entrenchment (7692001). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked, the refusal standing flatly, without qualifier of defiance or ease (7692002). Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are all absent: no degree of the refusal is scored, nothing narrows it, and no downstream outcome is booked to the operation - the whetted sword of the verse is read as the frame, not filed as this act's effect (present:false). Coupling (112) is 'refuse-to-repent' (inferred, to_span 283588): the one binding the reading registers is the weld of the interior to its own refusal - repentance and its rejection are the single fact here, the will locked shut (7692003). Prohibition (113) is absent: this is not a command but a description of a refusal. Discovery (114) names the placement: v12's 'if a man does not repent, God will whet his sword' reads the wicked's interior as a refusal to turn - the judgment hangs on that unrelenting inner posture (7692005). Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of the wicked's inner being, not a passing hesitation (7692006). Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the whole thing sits inside, a fixed condition of the inner life (7692004). The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the wicked man holds his interior shut against turning - a volitional refusal welded to itself, aimed at nothing but its own impenitence, reported without degree, and lodged wholly within as the settled inner posture on which the readied judgment hangs. This is repentance read at its dark pole: not the turning made but the turning refused.
narratives.story: This psalm pictures a righteous man appealing to a just God while a wicked enemy schemes against him. At its centre stands a warning about the wrongdoer's inner life: if a man does not repent. Repentance shows up here only as something the wicked man refuses to do. It is a matter of the will - not a feeling that overtakes him and not a single act he performs, but a turning he simply declines. The passage does not say what makes him this way; it just reports the closed door. His refusal is not aimed at anything beyond itself - it is entrenchment for its own sake, an interior locked shut. And it is a settled trait, not a passing mood. Everything about the judgment being readied over him - the sharpened sword, the bent bow - hangs on this one unmoving inner fact: he will not turn. This is repentance shown from its dark side: not the turn taken, but the turn withheld.
narratives.variation_note: The item 'repent' (H7725) carries two distinct readings in this family and the difference is the finding. Here at Psa 7:12 (H7725:repent#1) the word appears under negation and at its dark pole: the wicked's REFUSAL to turn, a volitional impenitence held by the evildoer, aimed at nothing but its own entrenchment, with judgment readied over it. At Psa 78:34 (H7725:repent#2) the same word is read positively as an actual turning-back to God by a chastened people - though a turning that later proved shallow. The one is the turn refused, the other the turn made-but-not-kept; set together they mark the two failure-shapes of repentance - never begun, and begun without root.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is haphak - 'You have turned my mourning into dancing' - a reversal worked upon the inner life, grief flipped to joy (7696945). Type (102) is affect: not a deed the self performs but a felt change of state, the emotional weather of the interior overturned (7696946). Source (103) is absent: the reading does not book a separate origin-event for the turning - though the verse names God as the one who turns, the source-row is left empty, so the reversal is reported as a received change rather than traced as an intake (present:false). Seat (104) is none: the reversal is not organ-located, not lodged in a named faculty - it is the whole inner person re-dressed, not one organ switched (7696947). Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred, to_span 276583): the first-person interior, the one brought up from Sheol who had mourned in sackcloth (7696948). Operation (106) is 'God turned the self's mourning into dancing, loosed its sackcloth and clothed it with gladness - the received reversal': the movement is a change done TO the interior, its grief exchanged for gladness like a change of clothes (7696949). Target (107) is transformation (inferred, to_span 276583): what the operation aims at is the transformation itself - the inner state remade, mourning becoming dancing (7696950). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked - the reversal is stated plainly, without qualifier of suddenness or degree (7696951). Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree of the change is scored, nothing narrows it, and no separate downstream outcome is booked - the reading holds the reversal itself as the whole event (present:false). Coupling (112) is 'mourning-to-dancing' (inferred, to_span 276583): the binding the reading registers is the very pairing of the two poles - mourning and dancing welded as the before and after of one motion, the sackcloth loosed and gladness put on (7696952). Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v11's 'You have turned my mourning into dancing; you have loosed my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness' - the operation is the felt reversal, the interior re-dressed from grief to joy (7696954). Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of the delivered self, the shape deliverance takes inside, not a fleeting flicker (7696955). Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the change is a condition of the inner life, felt within as the swing from grief to gladness (7696953). The full process: from no booked source-event and no organ-seat, the psalmist's interior is turned clean over - mourning exchanged for dancing, sackcloth for gladness - a received transformation of affect, welded as the pairing of its two poles, and lodged wholly within as the new inner state of the rescued. In a family whose word for turning usually names a human turning-back, this one names a turning-round done to the inner life.
narratives.story: This is a song of rescue. The psalmist had gone down to the edge of death and had mourned in sackcloth, and now he looks back at what happened to him: you turned my mourning into dancing. The turning here is not something he did but something done to him - his whole inner mood was flipped over, grief swapped for joy. The image is of changing clothes: the rough sackcloth of grief stripped off and gladness put on in its place. Mourning and dancing are held together as the two ends of a single motion, the before and the after. The passage does not linger on how it happened or measure it; it simply reports the reversal itself as the heart of the matter. And it is not a passing lift of spirits but the settled new condition of a rescued man. In a group of words mostly about people turning back to God, this one names the opposite direction - God turning a person's inner world right around.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is sug - 'They have all fallen away' - turning back, drawing off, apostatizing (7653101). Type (102) is action: a doing, the actual defection, not a mere mood (7653102). Source (103) is absent: the reading books no origin behind the falling-away, naming nothing that drove the race off, so the defection stands as bare universal fact (present:false). Seat (104) is none: the falling-away is not organ-located, not lodged in a named faculty - it is the whole person turned off, not one organ failing (7653103). Bearer (105) is all mankind (inferred, to_span 279906): and this is the reading's weight - the interior read is not one wicked man but the entire human race, 'the children of man' God looks down on (7653104). Operation (106) is 'turn back / fall away': the event is the collective drawing-off, mankind wheeling away from God (7653105). Target (107) is 'from God' (inferred, to_span 279906): the falling-away is away from God - he is the point departed from, the arena the defection turns its back on (7653106). Manner (108) carries a real value: 'all together, without exception' (inferred, to_span 279906) - the HOW is marked, and it marks the defection as total and unanimous, the whole race turning as one with not one left standing (7653107). Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no separate degree is scored beyond the totality already carried in the manner, nothing further narrows it, and no downstream outcome is booked (present:false). Coupling (112) is a span-resolved pair (from_span 279906 to_span 279908): the falling-away is 'paired with becoming corrupt together' - defection and corruption welded as one motion, to turn from God is in the same breath to rot (7653108). Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it starkly: 'they have all fallen away (sug)' is the universal human defection - the answer to God's search of v2, where he looks for any who understand and seek him: not one seeks, all have drawn back together (7653110). Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of mankind as such in this reading, not a lapse of a few (7653111). Locus (116) is external:god - the reference-point of the whole operation is God, the one turned away from; the movement is defined by its outward object (7653109). The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the entire human race turns off from God - a total, exceptionless defection welded to a shared corruption, aimed away from God as its point of departure, a standing characteristic of mankind read as God's own search comes back empty. This is the family's turning at its widest and darkest: not one soul turning back to God but every soul turned away.
narratives.story: This psalm takes God's own vantage point: he looks down from heaven over the whole human race to see if anyone understands, anyone truly seeks him. The verse gives the verdict - they have all fallen away. The word means turning back, drawing off, deserting, and here it is not one bad man but everyone, the entire race wheeling away from God at once. What makes it so heavy is the completeness of it: all together, without a single exception, not one left standing. And turning away is not a clean act - in the same breath they become corrupt; to desert God is to rot. The passage names no reason and traces no cause; it simply states the fact. This is the settled condition of humanity as the psalm sees it. In a group of words mostly about people turning back toward God, this one shows the opposite at its widest reach: everyone turned away, and God's search for even one who seeks him coming back empty.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is chaliphah under negation - 'because they do not change' - change named only as the thing the wicked will not undergo (7653856). Type (102) is status: not an act nor a feeling but a settled condition, the moral fixity of the enemies (7653857). Source (103) is absent: the reading books no origin behind the fixity, naming no driver for the refusal to alter, so the immovability stands as their bare state (present:false). Seat (104) is none: the not-changing is not organ-located, not lodged in a named faculty - it is the persons' whole standing condition, not one organ (7653858). Bearer (105) is the enemies (inferred, to_span 280116): the interior read is the treacherous company of the psalm, the smooth-tongued former friend and those with him (7653859). Operation (106) is 'do not change / will not repent' (inferred, to_span 280116): the event is a non-event, the interior refusing to shift course, entrenched in its way (7653860). Target (107) is none: the reading books no object the not-changing is aimed at - the fixity resolves to nothing beyond itself, a stasis with no target (7653861). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked - the refusal to change is stated flatly, without qualifier (7653862). Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, and no downstream outcome is booked (present:false). Coupling (112) is a span-resolved pair (from_span 280116 to_span 280118): the not-changing is 'paired with their not fearing God' - the fixity welded to the absence of the fear of God; the two are one root, immovability in evil growing precisely where there is no fear of God to move it (7653863). Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: 'because they do not change (chaliphah) and do not fear God' is the moral fixity of the wicked - obstinacy in evil, an unrepentance rooted in having no fear of God (7653865). Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of the enemies' inner being, not a passing stubbornness (7653866). Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the fixity is a condition of the inner life, an inward immovability (7653864). The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the enemies hold to a settled inner fixity - they will not change, a status aimed at nothing but its own stasis, welded to their lack of the fear of God, an inward immovability that is the very ground of their unrepentance. Here the family's language of turning appears as the turning that never comes: an interior that refuses to alter, because nothing in it fears the God who could alter it.
narratives.story: The psalmist is betrayed by a close friend whose words were smooth as butter while war was in his heart, and he looks at what such enemies are like inside. The verse names it: they do not change. Change here is the one thing they will not do - not a feeling, but a fixed condition, a moral hardness that refuses to shift. Their inner life is simply stuck, entrenched in its own way, aimed at nothing beyond staying as it is. And the passage puts its finger on why: they do not change and do not fear God. The two go together - the refusal to alter grows exactly where there is no fear of God to unsettle it. Take away that fear, and nothing is left to move them. This is a settled trait, not a passing stubbornness. In a family of words about turning, this is the turning that never happens: an inner life frozen in place because nothing in it stands in awe of the God who could thaw it.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is shuv - 'they repented' - a turning-back, the interior wheeling round toward what it had left (7664186). Type (102) is action: a doing, the actual turn made, not a mere feeling (7664187). Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior origin for the turn - though the verse shows it provoked by God's killing among them, the source-row is left empty, so the turning is reported as the act itself, its spring unfiled (present:false). Seat (104) is none: the turning is not organ-located, not lodged in a named faculty - it is the persons turning, not one organ (7664188). Bearer (105) is 'they' (inferred, to_span 283158): the interior read is the wilderness generation, the people who had eaten, been struck, and now turn (7664189). Operation (106) is 'turn back': the event is the return itself, the people wheeling back toward God under the blow (7664190). Target (107) is 'to God' (inferred, to_span 283158): the turning is Godward - he is the one turned back to, the point the return is aimed at (7664191). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked - the turn is stated plainly, though the discovery flags its shallowness (7664192). Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree of the turning is scored, nothing narrows it, and no downstream outcome is booked to the operation (present:false). Coupling (112) is 'paired with the seeking' (inferred, to_span 283158): the turning-back is welded to a seeking - 'they sought him... sought God earnestly'; the return and the search move together, turning expressed as earnest seeking (7664193). Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) is decisive and honest: 'they repented (shuv) and sought God earnestly' is the turning-back - though (v37) it proved shallow, a turn made but not held (7664195). Role (115) is characteristic: a trait of the people's inner response, here the recurring shallow turn (7664196). Locus (116) is external:god - the reference-point of the turning is God, the one returned to; the movement is defined by its Godward object (7664194). The full process: from no booked interior source and no organ-seat, the chastened people turn back to God and seek him earnestly - a real Godward action welded to their seeking, aimed at God as its object, yet (by the discovery's own honesty) a turning that did not last. Here repentance is read at its ambiguous middle: neither refused as in Psa 7 nor sustained, but begun under the blow and let go once the blow lifted.
narratives.story: This psalm retells Israel's history in the wilderness - fed, then struck down when they kept sinning. The verse catches a moment of turning: when God began killing among them, they repented and sought God earnestly. This is repentance as an actual movement - the people wheeling back toward the God they had abandoned. Their turning and their seeking are the same motion; to turn back is to search for him in earnest. And it is aimed squarely at God himself. But the passage is honest about what kind of turning it was. Only a couple of lines later it admits they flattered him with their mouths and lied to him with their tongues - the turn was real but shallow, made under the pressure of the blow and dropped as soon as the pressure eased. So this is repentance caught in the middle: not flatly refused, but not held either. It began when it hurt and faded when the hurt did.
narratives.variation_note: The item 'repent' (H7725) carries two distinct readings and the difference is the finding. At Psa 7:12 (H7725:repent#1) the word stands under negation as the wicked's flat REFUSAL to turn, an entrenched impenitence with judgment readied over it. Here at Psa 78:34 (H7725:repent#2) the same word is a real, Godward turning-back by a chastened people who seek him earnestly - but (v37) a turn that proved shallow, dropped once the chastening lifted. The one is repentance never begun; the other is repentance begun without root. Together they mark two ways the turn can fail: withheld, and unheld.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is sug - 'but turned away' - drawing off, wheeling back from God (7664384). Type (102) is action: a doing, the actual defection, not a feeling (7664385). Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior origin, naming no driver for the turning-away beyond the inherited pattern the discovery flags (present:false). Seat (104) is none: the turning-away is not organ-located, not lodged in a named faculty - it is the persons turning off, not one organ (7664386). Bearer (105) is 'they' (inferred, to_span 283330): the interior read is the same generation, now settled in the land yet turning off from the God who settled them (7664387). Operation (106) is 'turn away': the event is the defection itself, the people wheeling back from God after all his acts for them (7664388). Target (107) is 'from God' (inferred, to_span 283330): the turning is away from God - he is the point departed from (7664389). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked - the turning-away is stated plainly (7664390). Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, and no downstream outcome is booked to the operation (present:false). Coupling (112) is 'paired with acting treacherously' (inferred, to_span 283330): the turning-away is welded to treachery - 'turned away and acted treacherously'; defection and faithlessness are one motion, the turn expressing itself as betrayal (7664391). Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: 'but turned away (sug) and acted treacherously like their fathers' is the apostasy inherited from the fathers - a turning that runs in the line, the sons repeating the defection of the sons before them (7664393). Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of this people's inner life, and by the discovery a hereditary one (7664394). Locus (116) is external:god - the reference-point is God, the one turned from (7664392). The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the people turn off from God after all his deliverances - a defection welded to treachery, aimed away from God, and (by the discovery) inherited from their fathers like a twisted family trait. The verse's own image seals it: they twisted like a deceitful bow, a turning that cannot fly true. Here the family's turning is apostasy in the bloodline - the same drawing-off as Psa 53, but now specifically handed down.
narratives.story: After a long recital of God's rescues - leading them out of Egypt, bringing them into the land, driving out nations before them - the psalm turns to how the people answered: they turned away. The word means drawing off, deserting, and here it is the whole people wheeling back from the very God who had just settled them. Turning away and betrayal are one and the same motion; the desertion showed itself as treachery. And the passage marks something particular about it - they turned away like their fathers. This apostasy runs in the family line, the sons repeating the defection of the generation before them, handed down like an inherited flaw. The verse even likens them to a warped bow that cannot shoot straight. This is the same turning-away-from-God seen elsewhere, but named here as something bred in the bone, passed from fathers to sons.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is sug under negation - 'Then we shall not turn back from you' - the drawing-off named as the very thing vowed against (7665431). Type (102) is disposition: not a single act nor a felt spike but a settled bearing, a standing resolve of the interior (7665432). Source (103) is absent: the reading books no origin behind the resolve - though the verse conditions it on God's giving life, the source-row is empty, so the vow is reported as the bearing itself (present:false). Seat (104) is none: the not-turning-back is not organ-located, not lodged in a named faculty - it is the people's whole resolve, not one organ (7665433). Bearer (105) is 'we (the people)' (inferred, to_span 283738): the collective interior of the nation praying for restoration (7665434). Operation (106) is 'not turn away': the event is a vowed non-defection, the interior pledging to hold rather than draw off (7665435). Target (107) is 'from God' (inferred, to_span 283738): the not-turning is away from God negated - God is the one they vow not to depart from (7665436). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked - the vow stands plainly (7665437). Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, and no downstream outcome is booked (present:false). Coupling (112) is 'paired with calling on his name' (inferred, to_span 283738): the vowed fidelity is welded to invocation - 'we shall not turn back from you... and we will call upon your name'; not-turning and calling-on move together, fidelity expressed as prayer (7665438). Prohibition (113) is absent - this is a vow, not a forbidding. Discovery (114) names it: v18's 'Then we shall not turn back (sug) from you' is the vowed fidelity, the promise not to apostatize if God will but restore (7665440). Role (115) is characteristic: a standing disposition the people pledge to hold (7665441). Locus (116) is external:god - the reference-point is God, the one they vow not to turn from (7665439). The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the praying people vow a settled fidelity - not to turn back from God - conditioned on his reviving them, welded to their calling on his name, aimed at God as the one not-departed-from. Here the family's sug is inverted into promise: the same turning-away that Psa 78 and Psa 53 report as fact is here the very thing the interior binds itself against, fidelity defined precisely as the refusal to defect.
narratives.story: This is a prayer for a battered nation begging God to restore them. In the middle of it comes a vow about their own inner loyalty: then we shall not turn back from you. The turning-back they name is desertion, drifting away - and here it is exactly what they promise not to do. This is not a one-off act but a settled bearing they pledge to hold. Their promise not to desert is bound up with prayer: we will not turn back from you, and we will call on your name - staying loyal and calling on him are the same commitment. And it comes with a condition - if God will revive them and give them life, then they will hold. The same turning-away that other psalms report as hard fact is here flipped into a promise: loyalty defined as the refusal to drift, the people binding their inner life against the desertion they know they are capable of.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is shuv - 'but let them not turn back to folly' - turning named as the relapse warned against (7666827). Type (102) is disposition: not a single act but a settled bearing, the direction the interior is urged to keep or lose (7666828). Source (103) is absent: the reading books no origin behind the possible relapse, naming no driver, so the danger stands as a bare possibility guarded against (present:false). Seat (104) is none: the turning-back is not organ-located, not lodged in a named faculty - it is the persons' whole bearing (7666829). Bearer (105) is the saints (inferred, to_span 284237): the interior read is God's own people, the forgiven and restored to whom he speaks peace (7666830). Operation (106) is 'not turn back': the event is a relapse held off - the interior urged not to wheel back to what it left (7666831). Target (107) is 'to folly' (inferred, to_span 284237): the turning, were it to happen, would be back to folly - folly is the old state the relapse would return to (7666832). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked - the warning stands plainly (7666833). Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, and no outcome is booked (present:false). Coupling (112) is 'paired with the folly warned against' (inferred, to_span 284237): the not-turning-back is welded to the folly it must avoid - the disposition defined by the very thing it is to shun, peace held only by not reverting to folly (7666834). Prohibition (113) is absent as a distinct row, yet the whole reading is cast as a warning ('let them not') - the forbidding lives in the operation rather than in a separate prohibition item. Discovery (114) names it: v8's 'but let them not turn back (shuv) to folly' is the relapse guarded against, the danger that the restored might revert (7666836). Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait the restored interior must keep - fidelity as non-relapse (7666837). Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the turning-or-not is a condition of the inner life, sitting within as the restored self's bearing (7666835). The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, God's restored people are urged to hold a settled bearing - not to turn back to folly - the disposition welded to the very folly it must shun, aimed at the old state as the thing not to return to, lodged within as the inner posture of the forgiven. Here the family's turning is the peril of the pardoned: not the wicked's refusal to turn (Psa 7) nor outright defection (Psa 78) but the restored soul's risk of drifting home to its old folly, and the charge to hold.
narratives.story: This is a psalm of a people already forgiven and restored, listening for what God will say - and what he speaks is peace. But right alongside the promise of peace comes a quiet warning about their inner direction: let them not turn back to folly. The turning here is relapse - the danger that people who have been set right might drift back to the old foolishness they came out of. It is not a single slip but a whole bearing, a direction the restored heart has to keep. And the warning defines itself by exactly what it fears: peace is kept only by not returning to folly, so the folly they must avoid hangs over the charge. This is the peculiar risk of the pardoned. It is not the hardened refusal to turn, and it is not open desertion - it is the restored soul's temptation to wander back to where it started. The passage names that risk and urges them to hold their ground.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is shuv - 'Return, O my soul, to your rest' - a turning-back, here the soul called home to quiet (7679275). Type (102) is action: a doing, the summons to return enacted as a turn, not a mere mood (7679276). Source (103) is absent: the reading books no origin behind the summons - though the verse grounds it in the LORD's bountiful dealing, the source-row is empty, so the return is reported as the act of self-address itself (present:false). Seat (104) is none: the returning is not organ-located, not lodged in a named faculty - it is the whole self turned upon itself, not one organ (7679277). Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred, to_span 271002): the first-person interior, the one delivered from the snares of death who now speaks to his own soul (7679278). Operation (106) is 'return': the event is the soul's homecoming, the interior turning back to its rest (7679279). Target (107) is 'his soul to rest' (inferred, to_span 271002): the return is aimed at rest - the soul's own quiet, the peace it is called back into (7679280). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked - the summons stands plainly (7679281). narratives.story: This psalmist has just been pulled back from the edge of death - the snares of death had closed around him - and now, rescued, he speaks to his own soul: return, O my soul, to your rest. The turning here is a homecoming. He is not turning back from sin and not deserting anything; he is calling his own inner self back into quiet after the terror is over. It is something he does to himself, a self-summons to peace, grounded in the fact that the Lord has dealt generously with him. Everything about it points inward: the return and the soul's own settled condition are bound together, and the whole movement is fixed on that inner rest as its home. This is the gentlest turning in the family - not a refusal to turn, not a falling away, but a shaken soul told, now that the danger has passed, to come back home and be still.

narratives.story: In this long meditation on God's law, the psalmist describes a very deliberate inner move: when I think on my ways, I turn my feet to your testimonies. It starts with self-examination - he takes stock of how he has been living - and that reflection produces a turn. The turning is a change of direction in how he actually walks, his conduct swung around to point at God's word. And he does it without dragging his heels; the next line says he hurries and does not delay. This turn is not an isolated moment but one beat in the psalm's larger rhythm of turning toward God again and again. Its whole aim is outward, fixed on God's word as the thing he is turning to. This is the good turn shown plainly: a person who honestly looks at his own life and, because of what he sees, redirects his steps toward God.
narratives.variation_note: The item 'turn' (H7725) carries two distinct readings and the difference is the finding. Here at Psa 119:59 (H7725:turn#1) the psalmist himself is the bearer: reflecting on his ways, he turns his own feet to God's testimonies - a self-turning aimed Godward, located external:god (vertical, self to God's word). At Psa 119:79 (H7725:turn#2) the bearers are 'those who fear God' and the target is the psalmist: he prays that the faithful would turn toward HIM, located external:person (horizontal, community to a fellow servant). Same verb, same psalm, but the direction of the turning shifts from Godward to manward - evidence that shuv names a movement of alignment whose meaning is set by who turns and toward whom.

narratives.story: In this same long psalm, a few sections on, the writer prays a slightly surprising thing: let those who fear you turn to me. The turning here is not his own move toward God but other people's move toward him. He is asking that the God-fearing community would come and align themselves with him - and the reason is so that they, through him, may come to know God's ways. What makes this one stand out from the rest is its direction. Most of the turnings in this family point toward God or away from God; this one points toward a person, the psalmist himself. It is a sideways, human-to-human turning: the faithful gathering around a fellow servant who holds fast to God's word. So alongside the picture of a single soul turning to God, the psalm also imagines a community turning toward one another, drawn together around the one who keeps the testimonies.

narratives.story: Surrounded by enemies who set traps for him, the psalmist states his own steady inner course: I do not turn aside from your rules. The turning here is swerving off the path, and he names it only to say he refuses it. This is not a single act but a settled way of being - a constancy, a holding straight when everything around him would pull him off. What he refuses to veer from is God's word, and he gives the reason: for you have taught me. His steadiness is not sheer willpower but rests on the fact that God himself has been his teacher. It is one thread in the psalm's larger pattern of either turning away or holding fast. Here it is the good kind of not-turning: not the hardened refusal to repent, but the faithful refusal to drift - a person taught by God who simply will not swerve from what he has learned.

narratives.story: This short psalm contrasts two kinds of people: those who trust God, steady as a mountain, and those who go a different way. The verse names the second group by their inner direction - those who turn aside to their crooked ways. The turning here is a veering off, bending from the straight path onto twisted side-roads. It is set against the upright in heart just mentioned; these are the ones who bend away instead. The passage treats this not just as a wrong step but as a condition of the inner life - a bentness they carry inside. And it marks where such veering lands them: they are grouped with the evildoers, whom the Lord leads away. So the picture works on two levels at once - a crookedness within, and the bad company it ends in. This is apostasy shown quietly: not a loud desertion but the slow bending-off the straight road, and the fate that bending shares.

narratives.story: Near the end of this psalm about a God who knows him utterly - who formed him in the womb and whose thoughts toward him outnumber the grains of sand - the psalmist says something quietly remarkable: when I awake, I am still with you. This is not something he does; it is a condition he simply finds himself in. Sleep is a kind of gap, a nightly break in awareness, and the wonder is that when his mind comes back on in the morning, God is still there - the connection held straight through the dark. Waking and being-still-with-God are one and the same discovery: to come to is to realize he never left the presence. It is a settled feature of his inner life, an abiding with-God-ness that even unconsciousness cannot cut. In a family full of turnings - turning away, turning back, refusing to turn - this is the one that needs no turn at all: a self so continuously with God that waking only confirms the bond was never broken.
